newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Chronology of Serbian anti-government protests.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of Serbian anti-government protests.

text.p: Serbia's Socialist-led parliament voted a special law on Tuesday reinstating annulled opposition local election victories in 14 of the republic's 18 largest towns after 86 days of street protests.
Here is a chronology of related events:

Nov 17 - Second round of voting in municipal elections with Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition confident of success against ruling Socialists and their allies after good showing in Nov 3 first round.
Nov 18 - Zajedno claims victory in 14 towns including Belgrade. Demonstrations begin in southern Nis where Zajedno suspect authorities will overturn result.
Nov 19 - Belgrade electoral commission confirms Zajedno victory in capital but authorities, alleging " irregularities" begin to annul results in Nis and several other towns.
Nov 21 - 20,000 people march in Belgrade. Zajedno leaders vow daily protests until victory recognised. Socialists accuse Zajedno of inciting violence.
Nov 24 - Belgrade municipal court annuls opposition victory in city council.
Nov 25 - Students strike in Belgrade faculties. Some 100,000 opposition supporters attend Belgrade demonstration.
Nov 26 - Supreme Court rejects appeal from opposition lawyers on annulment of poll results.
Nov 28 - Socialists say they secured majority in Belgrade assembly after third round of voting which Zajedno boycotted.
Dec 3 - Authorities shut down independent radios and Washington says "outer wall" of sanctions against Belgrade will remain in place until Serbia respects for democracy.
Dec 4 - President Slobodan Milosevic's government promises Washington it will not use force to stop protests
Dec 5 - Belgrade rally draws 150,000; radios back on air.
Dec 6 - European Union refuses Serbia preferential trade.
Dec 8 - Belgrade electoral commission awards poll victory in the capital to the Socialists and their allies.
Dec 10 - Opposition boycotts federal parliament until Milosevic backs down. Federal supreme court rejects Zajedno appeal.
Dec 13 - Milosevic invites Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) delegation to assess elections.
Dec 20 - OSCE delegation led by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez arrives in Belgrade.
Dec 24 - Rival government, opposition rallies in Belgrade lead to street battles in which one man is shot in the head.
Dec 26 - Serbian Interior Ministry ban rallies that block traffic. Riot police force demonstrators off the streets.
Dec 27 - Gonzalez report backs opposition. Demonstrators clash with riot police.
Dec 31 - At least 250,000 people hold New Year rally, blowing whistles and ringing alarm clocks.
Jan 3 - Serbian authorities admit opposition won some disputed municipal elections but make no mention of Belgrade city assembly and say results unclear in other key cities.
Jan 5 - Demonstrators paralyse Belgrade with slow-moving car parade which gets round ban on street marches.
Jan 6 - Orthodox Christmas festivities bring biggest crowd onto streets. Bomb at leftist party building raises tension.
Jan 8 - Socialists concede Zajedno won Nis.
Jan 11 - Two Serbian deputy prime ministers accept opposition victories in the 14 towns.
Jan 14 - Half a million people jam central Belgrade on Orthodox New Year's Eve for biggest anti-government protest.
Jan 16 - OSCE chairman Helveg Petersen, the Danish foreign minister, says Socialists must recognise the election results and stop making "piecemeal" concessions.
Jan 18 - Riot police withdraw from central Belgrade after all-night stand-off with students, letting them march.

Jan 23 - Riot police club demonstrators in Kragujevac demanding Socialists relinquish control of regional television station; opposition member of parliament beaten unconscious in bloodiest confrontation involving protesters to date.
Jan 27 - Orthodox Church Saint Sava Day march in Belgrade, led by Serbian Patriarch Pavle, joined by more than 100,000 opposition demonstrators. Opposition take over in Nis.
Feb 2/3 - Security police attack demonstrators in Belgrade in overnight violence that is worst seen in capital since 1991 when Milosevic smashed protests with army tanks.
Feb 4 - Milosevic orders government to pass a law in parliament reinstating Zajedno victories but street protests continue to put pressure on him to keep his word.
Feb 6 - Zajedno says demonstrations to end after vote in parliament and plans dialogue with authorities.
Feb 11 - Socialist-led Parliament votes a special law to reinstate the Zajedno victories.
